data.name: 3D Arcade Fishing
data.detailed_description:
Feel like some seriously casual bit of fishing fun full of excitement? 3D Arcade Fishing will take you on an action-packed fishing adventure at stunningly beautiful locations all around the globe. Surrounded by nature's quiet beauty you experience your pulse shooting upwards as soon as your first or biggest fish finally bites. But now you have to stay calm to make sure the fish won't make a last minute escape.

Whether you're a weathered veteran or just started learning the ropes, this fishing adventure is easy to learn, but hard to master, and only the perfect mix of skill and patience make a champion. Every fish you catch increases your experience. Step by step you unlock new bait to lure in even bigger fish. Use the money you win to buy better equipment at the bait shop.

Will you manage to haul in even those fish that just won't bite?


  • 15 different locations: Test your skills at 3 different lakes full of fish with 5 fishing spots each, e.g. Loch Ness.
  • Improve your experience level and equipment: Increase your experience level to unlock better bait and buy new fishing equipment (hooks & rods) at the bait shop.
  • Many different kinds of fish: Haul in 11 different kinds of fish in various sizes and weights.
  • Simple, yet challenging game play: Simple controls and a low learning curve make for lots of casual fishing fun.
  • Different fishing champions to choose from: Choose from 9 different character models (6 male, 3 female).
  • Acoustic fishing guide: To help you find the perfect timing for casting your line and hauling it back in you can switch on an acoustic guide to help you.

reviews.review:
3D Arcade Fishing is a casual fishing game developed by bumblebee and published by familyplay together with Markt+Technik that focuses on creating a relaxing and accessible fishing experience built around simple mechanics, peaceful environments, and steady progression. Rather than attempting to simulate every technical aspect of real-world fishing, the game embraces a more arcade-oriented style designed for players who want calm gameplay mixed with light progression and enjoyable fishing challenges. Its approachable mechanics and relaxing atmosphere make it feel more like a comfortable recreational activity than a demanding sports simulation.

The game places players in a variety of scenic fishing locations spread across multiple lakes and outdoor environments inspired by real-world landscapes. Quiet waters, natural scenery, and calm environmental design immediately establish the peaceful tone that defines the entire experience. The atmosphere becomes one of the game’s strongest features because it successfully captures the relaxing side of fishing while still maintaining enough challenge to keep catches satisfying.

Gameplay revolves around selecting fishing spots, casting lines into the water, waiting for fish to bite, and carefully reeling them in before they escape. The mechanics are intentionally easy to understand, allowing even newcomers to begin fishing almost immediately without complicated tutorials or realistic simulation systems getting in the way. This simplicity helps the game remain approachable and low-pressure throughout most of the experience.

Despite its arcade-focused design, the game still introduces a satisfying sense of progression. Players earn rewards and experience from successful catches, gradually unlocking improved rods, hooks, bait, and fishing equipment capable of attracting larger and rarer fish species. Stronger fish require better timing and more careful control while reeling them in, creating moments of tension that break up the otherwise calm pacing effectively.

The variety of fishing locations also helps maintain interest during longer sessions. Different lakes contain unique environments and fish populations, encouraging players to experiment with different equipment and strategies depending on the area. Locations such as Loch Ness add a bit of personality and visual variety while giving players new places to explore as they continue progressing through the game.

Fish variety contributes heavily to the gameplay loop as well. Smaller catches are relatively easy to secure, but larger fish introduce more resistance and challenge during retrieval. Successfully landing a rare or powerful fish feels rewarding because players must balance patience and timing carefully to avoid losing the catch. These moments provide bursts of excitement that contrast nicely against the game’s slower and more peaceful atmosphere.

One useful feature is the optional acoustic fishing assistant, which provides audio cues to help players react at the correct moment during fishing sequences. This system makes the gameplay more accessible for beginners unfamiliar with fishing mechanics while also helping maintain the game’s relaxed pacing. The inclusion of optional guidance reinforces the idea that the experience is designed primarily around comfort and accessibility rather than strict realism.

Character selection offers a small amount of customization through multiple playable fishing champions featuring both male and female characters. While these choices do not dramatically affect gameplay, they help personalize the experience slightly and fit the game’s casual arcade identity.

Visually, 3D Arcade Fishing embraces bright colors and simple environmental design instead of aiming for photorealistic presentation. Lakes, forests, and water effects create pleasant scenery that supports the relaxing mood effectively even if the graphics themselves remain relatively modest by modern standards. The clean presentation works well because the game prioritizes atmosphere and accessibility over technical complexity.

The soundtrack and environmental audio further strengthen the calm tone. Gentle music, nature sounds, and soft water effects help create a peaceful outdoor atmosphere that makes the game ideal for slower play sessions. The audio remains subtle throughout, avoiding distractions while enhancing the feeling of spending time beside quiet lakes and rivers.

One of the game’s biggest strengths is how welcoming it feels for casual players. Controls remain simple, progression is straightforward, and the overall pacing avoids frustration. Players looking for a relaxing game to unwind with will likely appreciate the balance between light challenge and peaceful gameplay. The steady unlock system also gives enough motivation to continue improving equipment and searching for larger catches.

However, the same simplicity may leave hardcore fishing fans wanting more depth. Players expecting realistic fish behavior, advanced environmental simulation, or highly detailed customization systems may find the gameplay too repetitive and arcade-focused over time. The core mechanics remain relatively straightforward from beginning to end, meaning long-term enjoyment depends largely on personal appreciation for relaxed fishing gameplay.

Technical presentation is also somewhat limited compared to larger fishing simulators. Animations and environmental detail occasionally feel basic, and the gameplay loop may become repetitive during extended sessions. Still, the game’s modest scope allows it to remain focused and accessible without overwhelming players with unnecessary complexity.

3D Arcade Fishing ultimately succeeds as a relaxing and approachable fishing game that prioritizes comfort, accessibility, and steady progression over realism. Its peaceful environments, satisfying progression system, and easy-to-learn mechanics create a pleasant casual experience for players who simply want to enjoy the calming rhythm of virtual fishing without the demands of a hardcore simulation.

Rating: 6/10
